text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 1.88% today after oil prices dropped sharply on news that G7 nations plan to release diesel reserves to ease supply constraints in Europe and the Middle East. Brent crude fell below $100 a barrel on the report, which pressures refiner margins — the profit spread between what a refiner pays for crude oil and what it gets for selling refined products like diesel and gasoline. The stock had jumped nearly 7% just yesterday on elevated oil prices, so today's retreat reflects the reversal of that tailwind.

Refining utilization remains strong at 92.5%, and inventories of gasoline and diesel are moderate, so the move is purely tied to crude prices falling. A wider supply of diesel flooding the market would ease one of the key constraints pushing up fuel prices, which had supported refiner profitability over the past week.
